The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Sky's USDS stablecoin shrinks 35% as $1.5 billion exits reserves after illicit-finance report. USDS held its $1 peg as a large holder linked to Poloniex withdrew much of decentralized protocol Sky's USDC liquidity backing its stablecoins. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Trump's Democratic SEC pick suggests tokenization policy deserves full rule process. The U.S. Senate Banking Committee held a confirmation hearing for the two nominees — one from each party — as the administration rebuilds the markets regulators. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Anthropic gains after IPO, but pulls off highest levels. After opening at $111.50, ANT quickly slipped back under $100, still above its $83 offering price. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto for Advisors: Falling prices drove October’s 10% drop in institutional crypto exposure. The report adds another detail to the day's market picture. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Binance wins $6.5 billion feezing order against hackers behind crypto's largest theft. The crypto exchange said it has already replaced the stolen assets using its own funds and insurance reserves. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto traders vs. Wall Street: OKX’s Anthropic markets put IPO pricing to the test. The crypto exchange plans to launch tokenized Anthropic shares as its pre-IPO futures trade about 24% above the company’s $83 offering price. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $61,522 with a -1.24% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,739.15 with a -1.34% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Ethereum and Bitcoin spot ETFs snap lengthy outflow streaks with fresh inflows
items.description:
by  Editorial Team

After weeks of watching money walk out the door, US spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs finally caught a break. Both product categories recorded net inflows on June 4-5, ending outflow streaks that had lasted nearly half a month for Bitcoin and even longer for Ethereum.

The numbers themselves are modest. Bitcoin spot ETFs pulled in roughly $3.05 million in net inflows, while Ethereum spot ETFs attracted $19.30 million.

## Thirteen days of bleeding, then a trickle of relief [...] Add us on Google

After weeks of watching money walk out the door, US spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs finally caught a break. Both product categories recorded net inflows on June 4-5, ending outflow streaks that had lasted nearly half a month for Bitcoin and even longer for Ethereum.

The numbers themselves are modest. Bitcoin spot ETFs pulled in roughly $3.05 million in net inflows, while Ethereum spot ETFs attracted $19.30 million.

## Thirteen days of bleeding, then a trickle of relief [...] ## What this means for investors

Look at the asymmetry in the numbers for context. Bitcoin ETFs lost $4.4 billion over 13 days and gained back $3.05 million. That recovery represents less than 0.1% of what left. Ethereum’s $19.30 million inflow is more meaningful relative to its $9.78 billion AUM, but it still barely moves the needle after 17 days of outflows.

### Increased Transparency

Regulatory pressure forces exchanges to improve:

 Disclosure standards
 Proof-of-reserves reporting
 Consumer protections [...] Bitcoin is generally viewed as a commodity rather than a security, but related products like ETFs still fall under SEC oversight.

### Why does the SEC sue crypto exchanges?

The SEC alleges some exchanges operate as unregistered securities platforms, listing tokens that qualify as securities.

### Does regulation hurt crypto prices?

Short term, yes. Long term, regulation may increase stability and institutional trust.

items.title: Companies plan stablecoins under new law, but experts say hurdles remain
items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump on July 18 signed the GENIUS Act into law, setting federal rules and guidelines for cryptocurrency tokens pegged to the U.S. dollar known as stablecoins. This U.S. law, the first designed to facilitate crypto usage, could pave the way for the digital assets to become an everyday way to make payments and move money, experts said. [...] The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, for instance, is expected to issue rules to outline several risk management and compliance requirements. Under the new U.S. framework, the Treasury Department will have to issue a rule on foreign stablecoin regulatory regimes and their compatibility with the new U.S. framework.

"These things are going to have to phase in," said Aschettino.

(Reporting by Hannah Lang in New York; Editing by Richard Chang)

items.title: This Week in Crypto Law (October 25, 2026)
items.description:
##### The opinion editorial below was written by Michael Handelsman for Kelman.Law.

## This Week in Crypto Law

This week, regulators and courts focused on the infrastructure surrounding digital assets: tokenized securities, customer-fund safeguarding, stablecoin competition, and cross-border fraud. The developments below also illustrate the different legal effects of an examination priority, an agreed regulatory sanction, a newly filed civil complaint, and a criminal prosecution. [...] ## SEC Makes Tokenization a 2027 Examination Priority

On October 23, the SEC announced its fiscal year 2027 examination priorities. The Division of Examinations identified tokenization and evolving market infrastructure among the areas warranting heightened attention. It will examine clearing agencies’ controls relating to tokenization and review how entities subject to Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity address tokenized securities. [...] The priorities also extend to issues likely to affect digital-asset businesses indirectly. Examiners will review broker-dealer anti-money-laundering programs, cybersecurity, third-party service providers, trading systems, transfer agents’ use of emerging technology, and controls surrounding new products and business activities.
